newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Jackson emerges, angry at Prague tabloid.
newsitem.headline: Jackson emerges, angry at Prague tabloid.

text.p: Pop star Michael Jackson finally emerged from his Prague hotel suite on Thursday amid reports that he was considering cancelling his first concert in two years because of a front-page story in a local tabloid.

Concert organisers said late on Thursday that the launch of Jackson's three-month, four-continent "HIStory" tour would still go ahead, but that came after an emotional day for fans, many of whom travelled long distances to see their idol.

Jackson sent the hundreds waiting outside the hotel into a frenzy by occassionally waving from his eighth-floor window as hordes of fans and media waited for the reclusive star to take an expected tour of the ancient Czech capital.
But after visiting a toy store and bookshop on Wednesday wearing a silky black mask to block the city's notoriously polluted air, Jackson stayed in his hotel throughout Thursday.
Czech news agency CTK and local television stations quoted sources close to Jackson aides as saying the star was furious over a front page story in the Prague tabloid Blesk (Lightning).
The story, in Czech with accompanying photos, rehashes charges made by a boy in Los Angeles who accused Jackson in August 1993 of sexually molesting him, triggering a police investigation.
In January 1994, the boy dropped his civil suit against Jackson in a multi-million dollar settlement.

An official with the local promoters confirmed to Reuters that organisers were furious with Blesk and the newspaper's accreditation for the show might be cancelled, but the concert was on. Some 130,000 fans are expected at the concert on the sprawling Letna Plain near Prague Castle.
